Analyses 7 and 8 compare StimGate with two other ways of setting a gate,
$F_{\beta}$ and Tailgate. This page chooses the settings those two methods use. It
looks at a response probability of 0.2%, all three transformations, both
degrees of separation, and parent populations of 5,000 and 100,000 cells.

For Tailgate, the settings are the derivative tolerance and the bias added to
its cutpoint. For $F_{\beta}$, the setting is $\beta$. Each choice is compared with
the published default settings and with the settings Analyses 7 and 8 use now.

## Set-up

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tibble)
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(tidyr)
})

root_dir <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("DESCRIPTION")) "." else "..", winslash = "/")
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root_dir, "DESCRIPTION")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root_dir)

scripts_r_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "r")
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-runtime.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-plot-style.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-thesis-table.R"))

run_simulations <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_simulations",
  "RUN_SIMULATIONS",
  FALSE
))
run_plots <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_plots",
  "RUN_PLOTS",
  TRUE
))
analysis_dev <- .analysis_is_dev()
analysis_quick <- .analysis_is_quick() && !analysis_dev

simulation_seed <- as.integer(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "simulation_seed",
  "SIMULATION_SEED",
  60600L
))
if (is.na(simulation_seed)) {
  stop("simulation_seed must be coercible to an integer.")
}

devtools::load_all(root_dir, quiet = TRUE)

if (isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  .analysis_require_packages(c("cytoUtils", "openCyto", "flowStats", "simcyto", "ks", "reticulate"))
}

# Source simulation helpers in dependency order.
for (fn in c(
  "sim-misc.R",
  "sim-bandwidth.R",
  "sim-compare-freq_bs.R",
  "sim-compare-tune.R"
)) {
  source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, fn))
}
```

## Scientific settings

The data are simulated as in Analysis 7: one marker, negative cells centred at
zero and responding cells centred at `mean_pos`, with variance 1.5, then
transformed (Gaussian, skewed or gamma). The low and high separations are
Analysis 7's. In the stimulated tube 0.2% of the cells respond. The
unstimulated tube has background responders at 0.2 times that rate (0.04%) and
the same number of cells. The seeds differ from Analysis 7's, so the settings
are chosen on different simulated data from the data used to report results.

Only $F_{\beta}$ and Tailgate are run. Both use the same inputs as in Analysis 7:
$F_{\beta}$ compares the stimulated tube with its unstimulated tube, and Tailgate
gates the stimulated tube on its own. As in Analysis 7, when a method finds
no cutpoint (without an error), the gate is placed just above the highest
cell. Errors are kept as missing results.

Tailgate settings:

- **Tolerance.** Tailgate's cutpoint is the first point to the right of the
  main peak, after the steepest descent, where the slope of the density is
  flatter than the tolerance. cytoUtils' default tolerance is an absolute
  value, 0.01, which depends on the scale of the data. Analysis 7 uses
  `autoTol = TRUE`: a tolerance of 1e-2 times the steepest slope. The grid
  varies that fraction in half steps on a log10 scale, from 1e-6 to 1e-1, and
  keeps the absolute 0.01 for comparison. A smaller tolerance moves the
  cutpoint further right; if the density never becomes that flat, Tailgate
  finds no cutpoint and the gate falls back to just above the highest cell.
- **Bias.** The cutpoint is then moved up by the bias, as StimGate moves its
  gates up by its own bias. Analyses 7 and 8 now use the bias selected here, 0.15 (previously 0.1).

$F_{\beta}$ setting:

- **$\beta$.** $F_{\beta}$ picks the gate that maximises the $F_{\beta}$ score of the
  stimulated tube against the unstimulated tube. $\beta$ below 1 weights
  precision more than recall, which pushes the gate up; $\beta$ above 1 pushes
  it down. The published value is 0.8. The other $F_{\beta}$ settings stay at their
  published values (theta 2, moving-average width 10).

```{r}
#| label: scientific-settings
tune_settings <- .simTuneSettings()
sim_grid_full <- .simTuneGrid(simulation_seed, prob_response = 0.002, n_cell = c(5e3, 1e5))

# Datasets of 20 samples, each sample one unstimulated/stimulated pair. The
# dataset is the unit for uncertainty; draft runs use fewer datasets.
sim_size <- .analysis_sim_size()
n_sample <- 20L
n_iter <- c(final = 10L, draft = 3L)[[sim_size]]
# Samples of the first dataset whose gates are drawn.
n_hist_sample <- 4L
# Settings whose mean median F1 is within this of the best are compared on
# their estimates.
f1_tolerance <- 0.02
# F-beta keeps its published beta: the top-ranked beta gates more aggressively
# for little gain in F1.
fbeta_beta_used <- 0.8

sim_grid <- sim_grid_full
# Dev keeps one debugging scenario; quick keeps the smallest grid that still
# draws every figure.
if (analysis_dev) {
  sim_grid <- dplyr::filter(
    sim_grid, .data$transformation == "gamma", .data$mean_pos_setting == "low",
    .data$n_cell == 1e5
  )
  n_sample <- 2L
  n_iter <- 1L
  n_hist_sample <- 2L
} else if (analysis_quick) {
  sim_grid <- dplyr::filter(
    sim_grid, .data$transformation %in% c("gaussian", "gamma"),
    .data$mean_pos_setting == "low", .data$n_cell == 5e3
  )
  n_sample <- 3L
  n_iter <- 1L
  n_hist_sample <- 2L
}

path_fbeta <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "python", "fbeta.py")
if (isTRUE(run_simulations) && !file.exists(path_fbeta)) {
  stop("F-beta comparison script not found: ", path_fbeta)
}
```

Each scenario has `r n_iter` datasets of `r n_sample` samples, so
`r n_iter * n_sample` stimulated tubes. Tailgate is run with
`r length(tune_settings$tailgate$tol_rel) + 1L` tolerances and
`r length(tune_settings$tailgate$bias)` biases, and $F_{\beta}$ with
`r length(tune_settings$fbeta$beta)` values of beta, all on the same tubes.

## Simulation

```{r}
#| label: simulate
#| include: false
analysis_key <- .analysis_mode_key(c("sim", "tune-comparators"))
fig_key <- .analysis_mode_key("6-sim-tune-comparators")
# Files the thesis uses go to the projr "output-thesis" label
# (_output/thesis), in its appendix folder (quick/dev renders one level down).
thesis_parts <- c("appendix", "qmd6", fig_key[-1L])
dir_cache <- .analysis_cache_dir(analysis_key, root_dir, create = run_simulations)
path_results <- file.path(dir_cache, "results.rds")

cache_settings <- .simTuneCacheSettings(
  grid = sim_grid,
  n_sample = n_sample,
  n_iter = n_iter,
  settings = tune_settings,
  simulation_seed = simulation_seed,
  profile = list(
    analysis_dev = analysis_dev, analysis_quick = analysis_quick,
    sim_size = sim_size, n_hist_sample = n_hist_sample
  )
)

if (isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  # Datasets run in parallel; each has its own seed, so the number of
  # workers does not change the results.
  results <- .simTuneRunGrid(
    sim_grid, n_sample, n_iter, path_fbeta, tune_settings, n_hist_sample,
    workers = max(1L, .simGetCores()), root_dir = root_dir
  )
  .simTuneWriteCache(results, cache_settings, path_results)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-one-simulation
#| include: false
#| eval: false
sim_id_target <- 10L
rerun <- .simTuneRunScenario(
  dplyr::filter(sim_grid_full, .data$sim_id == sim_id_target),
  n_sample, n_iter,
  fbeta_env = .simCompareFbetaEnvironment(pathFbeta = path_fbeta),
  settings = tune_settings, n_hist_sample = n_hist_sample
)
```

## Collation

```{r}
#| label: collate
#| include: false
if (!isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  results <- .simTuneReadCache(path_results, cache_settings, analysis_key)
}
metrics <- .simTuneMetrics(results$scores)
summary_tbl <- .simTuneSummary(metrics)
rank_tbl <- .simTuneRank(summary_tbl, f1_tolerance = f1_tolerance)
compare_tbl <- .simTuneCompareSettings(rank_tbl, fbetaUsedBeta = fbeta_beta_used)
selected_tbl <- dplyr::filter(rank_tbl, .data$selected)
selected_lab <- function(m) {
  lab <- selected_tbl$setting_lab[selected_tbl$method == m]
  if (length(lab) == 0L) "none (no setting had a finite F1 in every scenario)" else lab
}
n_cell_vec <- sort(unique(sim_grid$n_cell))
```

## How the settings are chosen

Settings are judged on the **F1 score** of their gates against the simulated
labels, 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN): its median and its 10th and 90th percentiles over
the stimulated tubes of a scenario. The percentiles pool the tubes of all
datasets in a scenario (200 tubes), and the twelve scenarios count equally.
For each method, the settings whose mean median F1 is within `r f1_tolerance`
of the best are kept, and of those the one with the narrowest mean 10th-90th
percentile F1 interval is chosen (ties go to the higher mean 10th percentile).
Settings outside the F1 cut are listed by mean median F1. The estimated
frequencies (the 10th and 90th percentiles of the background-subtracted
frequency against the true 0.2%) are shown below for context but do not
enter the choice.

The table below lists the five best settings of each method by that rule;
the setting each method uses in the comparisons is in bold. It is a Quarto
table with a caption and label for the thesis. Its source, including the
scoped Typst block that draws the thesis's table rules (not shown in this
HTML), follows in a copyable block and is saved as
`appendix/qmd6/sim-tune-comparators-ranking.md` in the projr `output-thesis` folder
(`_output/thesis`), ready to paste into the thesis and cite as
`@tbl-stimgate-appendix-tune-comparators`.

```{r}
#| label: selection
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  cat("\n\n**F\u03b2 setting used:** \u03b2 ", fbeta_beta_used,
    " (published). The top-ranked setting, ", selected_lab("fbeta"),
    ", gates more aggressively for little gain in F1, so it is not used.\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("**Selected Tailgate setting:** ", selected_lab("tailgate"), ".\n\n", sep = "")
  rank_top <- .simTuneRankDisplay(rank_tbl, n = 5L, fbetaUsedBeta = fbeta_beta_used)
  .analysis_md_show(.simTuneMdTable(rank_top), file.path(
    .analysis_project_dir("output-thesis", thesis_parts, root_dir),
    "sim-tune-comparators-ranking.md"
  ))
  .analysis_report_table(rank_tbl, c(fig_key, "setting_rank.csv"),
    "Every setting of each method, averaged over scenarios, in selection order.",
    root_dir)
}
```

## Top-ranked against default settings

$F_{\beta}$'s top-ranked setting is shown for comparison; the comparisons use its
published $\beta$ (0.8). Each point is the median over the stimulated tubes of one scenario, and the
bar runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile. The reference settings are
$F_{\beta}$'s published $\beta$ (0.8); Tailgate with cytoUtils' default absolute
tolerance (0.01) and no bias; Tailgate with a relative tolerance of $10^{-2}$
and no bias ("Tailgate (default settings)" in Analysis 7); and Tailgate with
bias 0.1 (relative tolerance $10^{-2}$). A relative
tolerance is a fraction of the steepest slope of the density, and $10^{-2}$ is
Tailgate's automatic tolerance; an absolute tolerance bounds the derivative.
The legend lists $F_{\beta}$'s settings in one column and Tailgate's in the other, marking each method's default (published $F_{\beta}$, cytoUtils' Tailgate default) and selected setting.

### F1

A thesis version of this figure, drawn at the thesis text width (146.5 mm by
215 mm), is saved as `appendix/qmd6/sim-tune-comparators-compare-f1.pdf` (and
`.png`) in the projr `output-thesis` folder.

```{r}

  ), height = 22)
  # The thesis version, at the thesis text width.

      "sim-tune-comparators-compare-f1"

  )
}
```

### Paired differences within datasets

For each dataset, the median F1 and the median estimate under the top-ranked
setting minus those under each reference setting. The table gives the mean
over datasets and its standard error (datasets are independent; the tubes of a
dataset are not separate units here).

```{r}
#| label: dataset-differences
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  diff_tbl <- .simTuneDatasetDifferences(metrics, compare_tbl)
  .analysis_report_table(diff_tbl, c(fig_key, "dataset_differences.csv"),
    "Selected minus reference setting, per scenario: mean and standard error over datasets of the dataset median F1 and median estimate.",
    root_dir)
}
```

## Gates

### On a subset of samples

The first `r n_hist_sample` samples of the first dataset in each scenario
(chosen in advance). Bars are the stimulated tube, with simulated responders
(orange) stacked on the negative cells (grey); the dark outline is the
unstimulated tube. Counts use a pseudo-log scale so that the few responding
cells stay visible. Vertical lines are the gates of the compared settings;
selected settings are dashed, so they remain visible where they give the same
gate as a reference setting.

```{r}
#| label: fig-gates
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 6.3
#| fig-height: 6.5
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  scen_tbl <- dplyr::distinct(sim_grid, .data$sim_id, .data$transformation,
    .data$mean_pos_setting, .data$mean_pos, .data$n_cell)
  for (trans in unique(scen_tbl$transformation)) {
    .analysis_heading(trans, 4L)
    for (i in which(scen_tbl$transformation == trans)) {
      row <- scen_tbl[i, ]
      .analysis_heading(paste0(
        row$mean_pos_setting, " separation (", row$mean_pos, "), ",
        .simTuneCellLab(row$n_cell)
      ), 5L)
      p <- .simTunePlotGates(
        dplyr::filter(results$hist, .data$sim_id == row$sim_id),
        dplyr::filter(metrics, .data$sim_id == row$sim_id),
        compare_tbl
      )
      .analysis_print_save_fig(p, file.path(
        .analysis_fig_dir(c(fig_key, "gates"), root_dir),
        paste0("gates-", row$transformation, "-", row$mean_pos_setting,
          "-n_cell_", format(row$n_cell, scientific = FALSE), ".png")
      ), height = 17)
    }
  }
}
```

## Tailgate: tolerance and bias

selected setting. Tolerances are fractions of the steepest slope, except
"abs 0.01", cytoUtils' default absolute tolerance.

## Coverage

Errors and fallback gates, by scenario and setting. A fallback gate sits just
above the highest cell, because the method found no cutpoint.

```{r}
#| label: coverage
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  coverage_tbl <- summary_tbl |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(.simTuneScenarioCols, "method", "setting_lab")),
      "n", "n_datasets", "n_error", "n_fallback", "n_f1_finite", "n_est_finite")
  .analysis_report_table(coverage_tbl, c(fig_key, "coverage.csv"),
    "Tubes, errors, fallback gates and finite F1 and estimates for every scenario and setting.",
    root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(summary_tbl, c(fig_key, "summary.csv"),
    "Median and 10th/90th percentiles of F1 and of the estimates for every scenario and setting.",
    root_dir, quiet = TRUE)
}
```

```{r}

```
